decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 1.5% to 1.75%. The vote was 8-2. Dissenting: Esther L. George, Eric S. Rosengren.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports remain weak.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed.

changes.quote: Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability.

tone_quotes.quote: In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.13% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.78% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.69% would fall by about $10.15 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.5%, and employers added an average of 176k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (September 2019); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.33%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.16% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 89%, cut 10%, hike 1%.
